P1.evidence: The application was read but only referenced twenty minutes in, during the presentation: 'because I saw in your application, you work like 10, 12 hours a day sometimes.' Nothing was read back at the open. The frame covered two of four parts: 'go. Where you're at at the moment, where you want to go. See if we can help you cross that bridge.' Agreement obtained. Open question asked verbatim.

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch — seven of nine addressed. 'So you're 185 pounds at the moment. How tall are you actually? I'm 5'6". And how old are you? 39.' Work asked and the 12-16 hour night-shift pattern established. Injuries asked twice, including 'Any other injuries that we should know about?' which surfaced the wrist. Training days asked. Results probed in detail (25 lb to 40 lb, 53 lb swings, 20 lb lost). Diet and energy both asked and probed. The single significant miss is sleep, never asked of a man working 7pm to 7am shifts.

P3.evidence: The deepest goals work in the batch. The bridge ran — 'why is getting to that next level to you so important?' — and produced kids, work capability and preventative maintenance. When the future-state answer came back vague, the rep pushed: 'what does amazing mean to you?' P3g landed properly and was then reinforced: 'when you're running around with your kids and ten years from now, your mobility is absolutely perfect still.' P3f is only partial because the kids were volunteered rather than drawn out with the scripted question.

P4.evidence: 'have you ever worked with a trainer before?' then 'And online trainers? Ever looked into doing something with someone like that?' then 'Why not?' Past attempts, what happened and why he never went further were all covered. He named the gap himself twice — 'my problem is I see so many videos and I want to try everything at once' and 'right now I'm kind of just going at it blind.' P4f could not run in its scripted form because he is sticking to it on his own, which is exactly why the value case stayed thin.

P5.evidence: P5a and P5b were bundled and P5a was very soft: 'when you're looking into the future and things would stay the exact same as they are at the moment, like, you're making improvements, but your mobility still isn't 100% on point.' P5b landed cleanly — 'do you feel like you're willing to settle for a life that you have at the moment without any improvements in the next six months, 12 months?' — and he answered 'no, I see myself wanting to improve as much as possible.' Then no why-not and no line in the sand. On a prospect who is already succeeding alone, nothing was ever made to cost anything.

P6.evidence: P6a ran cleanly and got a yes. P6b tested effort rather than commitment: 'are you going to put in 100% the effort to actually stick to the plans that he's going to make?' — '100%.' Money and the wife were never touched. P6c fails on the second half of the check: hesitation surfaced hard — 'I don't know if I'm going to be able to do this right now' — and instead of returning to Phase 5 the rep went to a holding deposit.

P11.evidence: No programme payment was collected — only a $100 refundable holding deposit. The 9am appointment booked is a follow-up sales call with Richard, not the Trevor onboarding. No agreement was sent or signed. The onboarding form was sent and the prospect was asked to complete it before any purchase, which is Phase 11 material used as a pre-commitment device.

objection_plays.detail: The most completely run objection play in the batch. Money aside test ran: 'outside of the investment, do you feel like, yeah, Richard, I do want to get started with this?' Obstacle anticipation ran: 'when you're going to say everything that we've just talked about to her, what do you feel like her response would be overall?' The permission-versus-input question ran in a softened form: 'is it sort of a thing that comes up for you too or is it mainly something that you feel like that's just a rule that we have together?' Support framing ran: 'I feel like she would support you in that sense, right?' The deposit-and-discuss close ran and the deposit was collected. The one scripted move that did not run is the responsibility challenge — 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house, is that responsibility hers or yours' — and the rep in fact validated the joint rule with 'That's understandable. I totally get that.'

Monthly leftover was asked and answered ('At least a couple grand'), credit score was asked by band ('Sevens'), and both third-party financing over 12 payments and three interest-free in-house payments were offered. Never ran: the isolation move in its scripted form before the money conversation, cash on hand, how many credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, crypto or investments. The rep also surfaced a $2,000 monthly surplus and then did not use it.

The rep named the uncertainty himself: 'Could it be that there's a little bit of uncertainty coming up?' and followed with 'Is it worth it?' None of the scripted moves ran — no certainty question, no pleasure-versus-pain framing, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before.

Trigger present: 'maybe right now is not the best time for me to put out all that money.' No scripted move ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets'. The rep treated it as a money objection rather than a timing one.

notes: Phases 2, 3 and 4 were the strongest in the batch and the whole call turned on Phase 5, which never made anything cost anything — and on this prospect that mattered most, because he is already losing weight on his own with free content. Objection play OB was run almost to the letter, which is worth crediting. The judgement to review is not adherence but the deposit: it is a scripted move, and it was applied to a man who had already withdrawn, cited a daughter in therapy and predicted his wife would refuse.
